answer: A knoll of trust can be built by requiring every agent to lock a refundable stake before it may transact; the stake is slashed if the agent is caught running duplicate identities. The ledge between honest and fake actors is the cost curve: one identity is cheap, but each extra identity multiplies the locked capital, so a Sybil farm must fund thousands of stakes to sway a market. Rotating saffron audit beacons - random spot-checks demanding live proof of unique hardware or recent work - raise the marginal cost further, since a botnet cannot fake time-bound proofs for every clone at once.
